full_judgment: 3. The facts of the case, in short, are that the plaintiff-petitioners filed Title Suit No. 82 of 1998 for permanent injunction and mandatory injunction stating, inter alia, that the landed properties recorded in CS plot Nos. 657, 671 and 672 of CS Khatian No.5168 described in the schedule 'A' in the plaint originally belonged to Rajani Mohan Kaibarta Das, Monhar Kaibarta Das and Radhika Mohan Kaibarta Das and CS Khatian was prepared correctly accordingly. Monohar Kaibarta Das died childless, subsequently Radhika Mohar Kaibarta Das and the sons of late Rajani Mohan Kabibarta Das transferred the entire property described in schedule 'A' to lndramati Dasya by a registered deed dated 9-10-1933 and in the petty settlement operation the name of Indramati Dasya was correctly recorded who paid usual land revenue to the Khashmohal Department of Dhaka Collectorate, after the petty settlement operation lndramati Dasya constructed houses on the eastern portion of the land of CS plot No. 657 and sold a portion of her purchased land to one Puma Lakshmi Dasya who died leaving behind a son Jugal Kishore Das as the only heir who sold his portion to Radhika Mohan Kaibarta Das. Subsequently a certificate case was started against Puma Lakshmi Dasya showing her single tenant for realisation of arrear rent and one Afia Khatun purchased the entire schedule property in auction; that Indramati Dasya filed Title Suit No. 48 of 1953 in the Court of 6th Munsif, Dhaka for declaration of her title and interest and for recovery of khas possession of the 'A' schedule property against the auction purchaser Afia Khatun and Government and obtained decree on compromise as the plaintiffs and defendants filed a joint compromise petition in the Court where auction purchaser Afia Khatun admitted that the certificate case was a nullity against the dead person and handed over possession of the properties to the substituted plaintiffs Chittaranjan Das, Monoranjan Das and Kesab Ranjan Das, who were the legal heirs of Late Indramati Dasya. Thereafter Chittaranjan Das and Kesab Das transferred entire 'A' Schedule properties by a registered permanent lease deed dated 6-10-1956 to one Abdus Salam Mia who has been possessing the entire 'A' schedule land by purchase and also by adverse possession for more than 12 years and transferred the same to Abdul Hashem on 21-5-69 by a registered sale deed.
